name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbency advantage with no outside spending against him
model.rationale: Brandon Gill holds a heavily Republican seat, has raised over $4.2 million against a Democratic opponent with under $20,000, and faces no outside opposition spending. Markets price his reelection at 98%, and no polls or expert ratings suggest any competitive threat.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising surge would be the only plausible path to competitiveness.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Texas's 26th District leans firmly Republican, and first-term incumbent Brandon Gill is running for reelection with overwhelming financial advantages. He has raised about $4.2 million and holds $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Steven Shook has raised roughly $17,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Gill, and no independent polls of the race exist.

Prediction markets give Gill about a 98% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the seat as competitive. With a double-digit partisan lean, an incumbent advantage, and a lopsided money gap, the race is rated Safe Republican. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor in the outcome.
